primitives.name: Compositional Isomorphism
primitives.verbatim_quote: The reference boards ARE the design: a generic board guarantees a generic site, and no amount of code craft recovers from it.
primitives.assumptions: Design fidelity is preserved under isomorphic transformation of visual elements.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When visual abstraction fails to maintain semantic alignment with intended user experience.

layer2.mapping: Each reference board maps to a unique visual configuration that preserves functional semantics across sections.
layer2.telemetry: Consistency score of visual motifs across rendered boards.

primitives.name: Asynchronous Rendering Pipeline
primitives.verbatim_quote: Submit all boards as async jobs at once (no `--wait`; collect the printed job ids), keep working while they render, poll `higgsfield generate wait <id>` / `higgsfield generate get <id>`, download into the repo's `refs/` directory (working artifact — NOT `app/public/`).
primitives.assumptions: Parallel processing increases throughput without compromising quality.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When synchronization errors cause race conditions in artifact retrieval.

layer2.mapping: Pipeline execution state is derived from job ID polling and artifact validation.
layer2.telemetry: Average time-to-render per board and success rate of artifact download.

primitives.name: Combinatorial Design Pick
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## The combinatorial pick (commit BEFORE prompting) To avoid the AI defaults, pick ONE option per category, write the pick into `app/design-brief.md`, and hold it across ALL boards.
primitives.assumptions: Fixed categorical selections ensure stylistic coherence across all visual outputs.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When inconsistent choices across categories introduce visual dissonance.

layer2.mapping: Each selected category defines a fixed parameter set used uniformly across all boards.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of adherence to predefined categorical selections.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that reference boards function as deterministic encoders of design intent, where each board represents a unique instantiation of a higher-order compositional schema. This schema is defined by a tuple of discrete choices drawn from predefined categories—theme, background, typography, architecture, etc.—which collectively form a combinatorial space. The isomorphism between these choices and their visual manifestation ensures that the final site inherits a consistent aesthetic logic. Asynchronous rendering enables parallel exploration of this space, while the combinatorial pick enforces a coherent baseline. Failure modes arise when the design space is underspecified or when the rendering pipeline lacks error handling, leading to inconsistent or broken outputs.
